miniAppNote.title: Telegram and MAX
miniAppNote.text: A custom app works in two messengers at once: Telegram and MAX, a Russian messenger. One price: we write the app once for both. The industry app includes only Telegram; you can add a MAX version for {max}. For that, you register your company in MAX (we send step-by-step instructions) and we connect the rest. Then MAX reviews the app. MAX decides how long the review takes, so that time is not part of our deadline.

pricing.caseOffer: We are a new studio and we need examples of our work. So we do our first five projects at the “case-study price” (a case study is an example of our work): development is 30% off. The discount is taken from the development price in the contract. Options, MAX and support are at the regular price. We will tell you how many spots are left when we reply to your request. In return we ask for two things. First, you let us show your site as an example of our work, without your customers' data. Second, you write an honest, detailed review of working with us, good or bad. We send you the link to the review form. Send the review before the acceptance certificate is signed: tell us how the work went. What changed after launch you can add later. The prepayment and the second payment are calculated from the regular price, and the discount comes off the final payment. No review by the acceptance certificate means no discount. If you later ask us to take down the review or the case study, we will. The contract says what happens to the discount then.
pricing.basicsHeading: Included in the price of every site
pricing.basicsNote: 13 items in the price; hosting and domain are paid to the provider directly. Telegram apps, 3D and support have their own lists on their pages

basics.code: We write the site ourselves, in code on Next.js, rather than putting it together in a website builder like Tilda
basics.lighthouse: Google's speed test on a phone: 90 out of 100 or more in each of three runs in a row, or we don't hand the work over. On launch day we test again, this time on your address: that result goes into the acceptance certificate. Third-party widgets, such as booking, maps or chat, slow a site down. If you chose them, we tell you before the contract what score we promise
basics.responsive: The site is easy to view on any screen: from a small phone (320 pixels wide) to a large monitor (1920 pixels)
basics.seo: We get the site ready for search. We add behind-the-scenes descriptions for search engines (schema.org) and for AI assistants (llms.txt). And a preview, a picture with a title that shows up when someone sends a link to the site in a messenger (OG). We do not promise a place in search results
basics.forms: Every lead goes to Telegram and email
basics.analytics: We connect GA4 and Yandex Metrica, the site analytics services. You see how many leads came in and from where: ads, social networks or search. Run an ad and you will see whether it brings leads from the site. Only visitors who allowed analytics in the cookie window at the bottom of the site are counted
basics.privacy: A cookie banner and a privacy policy. Before the contract we tell you what else you need to do yourself, for example under data protection law
basics.hosting: We set up the domain, a secure connection (SSL) and hosting and hand them over to you. You pay for the domain and hosting directly: the hosting provider monthly, the domain registrar once a year. Paid services, such as an online booking service, are also on you. Before the contract we work out what that comes to for you per year
basics.sources: We hand over the source code: all the files your site, admin panel and app are built from. With them you can change the site and move to another developer without us
basics.revisions: Three rounds of revisions included. A round is all your comments in one list, and we make all of it. Revisions are texts, photos, the color of individual blocks and buttons, the order of blocks; new pages, features and a whole new style are separate work
basics.warranty: A one-year warranty from the day of acceptance. We fix for free anything that broke through our fault or does not work the way the contract says. If the site stops opening through our fault, we get on it within 2 hours on weekdays from 10:00 to 19:00 Moscow time, and at night or on weekends the first working morning. Other bugs we start fixing within a working day and fix within 5 working days. If it is unclear whose fault a breakdown is, we first look for the cause for free and show it to you. Not covered: outages at the hosting provider and in third-party services (such as Telegram or a booking service) and breakdowns after changes to the site's code made by you or other people; such fixes cost $90 an hour. Texts and photos you change through the admin panel do not void the warranty.
basics.training: An admin panel, where you change texts, photos and prices yourself, and add or remove items: dishes, services, doctors. A guide and a screencast: how to work in the admin panel and read leads and analytics
basics.deadline: The deadline goes into the contract. If we are late through our fault, we cut the price by 2% for each day of delay, 20% at most. That amount comes off the final payment. It is calculated from the price of all the work in the contract, options included. If together with the case-study discount this exceeds the final payment, we refund the difference within 5 working days after the acceptance certificate

process.heading: How we build a one-page site in 4 days
process.contractNote: We fix all four in the contract

brief.title: Choosing a style and the top of the home page
brief.text: Before the contract is signed, we send a list of what the site needs, such as texts, photos and a logo. No texts of your own? We write them from a questionnaire and a conversation with you. That is included in the price, but the deadline grows by 2 days. We still show the styles 2 working days after the prepayment, with headings from the questionnaire, and write the texts once you pick a style. By the date in the contract we need the 30% prepayment and the materials from the list. Paid but did not gather the materials in time? We move the start to the nearest free date. The prepayment is not lost. After the prepayment we draw the top of your home page in three styles: colors, fonts, the look of buttons and blocks. You pick one. We show three styles 2 working days after the prepayment and the materials, and three more 2 working days after your reply. These dates also go into the contract, and for each working day we are late with the styles we also cut the price by 2%, within the same overall cap of 20%. You can also take a ready-made style: one of the five styles of this site or the style of our demo. None of the three fit? We draw three more. None of those fit either? We refund the whole prepayment. The deadline starts the day you pick a style: that is day 1. On that day we build the top of the home page in the chosen style, the part people see first. It is already a working page you can open on your phone. You send your comments in one list: that is the first of three rounds of revisions. Comments on the rest of the page come in the second and third rounds.

concept.title: The whole site on a temporary link
concept.text: We make your first-round revisions and build the whole site: every section, the form where customers leave requests, and visitor analytics. For now the site opens on a temporary link, so you can review it before launch. You send the second list of comments.

staging.title: Revisions and the speed test
staging.text: We make your second-round revisions. We set up analytics: GA4 counts the leads from the site, and tags in links show which ad or social network a visitor came from. We check the pages listed in the contract with Google's free speed test on a phone: each needs 90 out of 100 or more. If a page scores lower, we keep working at our own expense. We show you the result, you make the second payment of 40% and send the third and final list of comments.

launch.title: Launch and a one-year warranty
launch.text: We make your third-round revisions. We move the site to your web address (domain): now everyone can see it. We test the speed again, this time on your address. If it is below 90 there, we find the cause and show it to you. We set up the hosting, so if on launch day the site is slow because of the hosting, that is our concern: we fix it for free. If a third-party widget you chose slows the site down, we already told you before the contract what score we promise. We hand over all the passwords and files of the site: it is fully yours. You sign the acceptance certificate, the document that confirms the work is accepted, with the result of this test attached. After acceptance you pay the final 30%. Then comes a one-year warranty from the day of acceptance: we fix for free anything that broke through our fault or does not work the way the contract says. If it is unclear whose fault a breakdown is, we first look into it for free and tell you the cause. If the cause is not in our work, we first name the price of the repair, never charge more than that, and fix it only if you agree. Outages at the hosting provider itself are not covered by the warranty.

faq.question: How is a site for your industry different from “Start”?
faq.answer: “Start” is a one-page site. The site for your industry has several pages with sections and features for your industry. For each industry on the list we have a demo, an example of a finished site. We take its structure: the sections and features your industry needs, such as a menu with filters for a cafe or doctors with prices for a clinic. The design is drawn for you: three styles to choose from, as in “Start”. If you like the style of the demo itself, you can take it. Either way the site is yours: with your texts, your photos and on your address. The site for your industry costs more than “Start” and takes longer: it has several pages and features for your industry, while “Start” is one page. It has as many pages as the demo for your industry; a new page is separate work. For a clinic we add a notice about contraindications and the license details, and you are responsible for the medical texts. The deadline is {term}.

faq.question: My industry is not on the list. What now?
faq.answer: Then the landing page or the business website is a better fit. Take the quote quiz and we will suggest the right plan from your answers.

faq.question: How many days does a site for your industry take?
faq.answer: In {term}. We count calendar days, weekends included. The deadline starts the day you pick the style of the site, and it is set in the contract. We show three styles 2 working days after the prepayment and the materials. If we write the texts, the deadline is 2 days longer. Days we spend waiting for your comments don't count: the delivery date moves by the same number of days. There is no need to rush your reply. If a pause drags on for a long time, the contract says what happens next. If we are late through our own fault, we cut the price by 2% for each day of delay, 20% at most. That amount comes off the final payment. If together with the case-study discount this exceeds the final payment, we refund the difference within 5 working days after the acceptance certificate.

faq.question: Can I add features later?
faq.answer: Yes, even after launch, as options at extra cost: online payments, a quiz for your clients, reviews, messengers, a second language, CRM. What each option does and what it costs is in the “Options” list on this page.

faq.question: What if I don't like the design?
faq.answer: The style of a site is its colors, fonts and the look of its buttons and blocks. You choose it before the work starts. 2 working days after the prepayment and the materials, we show the top of your home page in three styles. You pick one. If you like, you can take a ready-made style instead: one of the five styles of this site (the “Style” button switches them) or the style of one of our demos. Then we don't draw it separately. The price stays the same. Another client may choose the same ready-made style, while a style drawn for you is yours alone. None of the three fit? Within 2 working days we draw three more. None of those fit either? We refund the whole prepayment and close the contract. The site deadline starts the day you pick a style.

Comments on the rest of the page come in the second and third rounds.

process.title: The whole site on a temporary link
process.text: We make your first-round revisions and build the whole site: every section, the form where customers leave requests, and visitor analytics. For now the site opens on a temporary link, so you can review it before launch. You send the second list of comments.

process.title: Revisions and the speed test
process.text: We make your second-round revisions. We set up analytics: GA4 counts the leads from the site, and tags in links show which ad or social network a visitor came from. We check the pages listed in the contract with Google's free speed test on a phone: each needs 90 out of 100 or more. If a page scores lower, we keep working at our own expense. We show you the result, you make the second payment of 40% and send the third and final list of comments.

process.title: Launch and a one-year warranty
process.text: We make your third-round revisions. We move the site to your web address (domain): now everyone can see it. We test the speed again, this time on your address. If it is below 90 there, we find the cause and show it to you. We set up the hosting, so if on launch day the site is slow because of the hosting, that is our concern: we fix it for free. If a third-party widget you chose slows the site down, we already told you before the contract what score we promise. We hand over all the passwords and files of the site: it is fully yours. You sign the acceptance certificate, the document that confirms the work is accepted, with the result of this test attached. After acceptance you pay the final 30%. Then comes a one-year warranty from the day of acceptance: we fix for free anything that broke through our fault or does not work the way the contract says. If it is unclear whose fault a breakdown is, we first look into it for free and tell you the cause. If the cause is not in our work, we first name the price of the repair, never charge more than that, and fix it only if you agree. Outages at the hosting provider itself are not covered by the warranty.

faq.question: How is “Business” different from “Start”?
faq.answer: “Business” has up to seven pages, while “Start” has one. There is a blog, a section for news and articles. A version of the site in a second language can be added for an extra fee. The admin panel, where you change texts, photos and prices yourself, comes with both “Business” and “Start”. “Business” differs from the site for your industry in that we design the pages and features for you from scratch rather than taking them from a demo. That is why it suits any business, not only a clinic, a cafe or an expert.

faq.question: Can I edit the texts myself?
faq.answer: Yes, in the admin panel. We send a guide and a screencast: how to change texts, photos and prices and read leads. If we put in temporary stock photos, you replace them with your own through the admin panel. Your edits through the admin panel do not void the warranty. The site shrinks the photos you upload on its own, so the speed doesn't drop.

faq.question: What if I need more than seven pages?
faq.answer: Each page beyond seven is priced separately: the price depends on how much work it takes. We name the amount before work starts.

faq.question: How many days does the “Business” site take?
faq.answer: {term}. The deadline starts the day you pick the style of the site, and it is set in the contract. We show three styles 2 working days after the prepayment and the materials. If we write the texts, the deadline is 4 days longer. Days we spend waiting for your comments don't count. If we are late through our own fault, we cut the price by 2% for each day of delay, 20% at most, and take it off the final payment. If together with the case-study discount this exceeds the final payment, we refund the difference within 5 working days after the acceptance certificate. Three rounds of revisions are included: three times you send a list of comments, and we make all of it.

faq.question: What if I don't like the design?
faq.answer: The style of a site is its colors, fonts and the look of its buttons and blocks. You choose it before the work starts. 2 working days after the prepayment and the materials, we show the top of your home page in three styles. You pick one. If you like, you can take a ready-made style instead: one of the five styles of this site (the “Style” button switches them) or the style of one of our demos. Then we don't draw it separately. The price stays the same. Another client may choose the same ready-made style, while a style drawn for you is yours alone. None of the three fit? Within 2 working days we draw three more. None of those fit either? We refund the whole prepayment and close the contract. The site deadline starts the day you pick a style.

faq.question: Will a “Business” website work for a clinic?
faq.answer: Yes. We design the pages around your clinic: doctors, services and prices, for example. Russian Health Ministry Order No. 118n lists what a clinic website must have. Of that, we build three things at no extra cost: a version for the visually impaired, site search and a form where patients rate the quality of care. “Business” has up to seven pages. The form and search do not count toward them, and the page with the clinic information the order requires is one of the seven. The rest of what the order requires on the site, such as your license and doctors' details, we add from your documents, and after that you change doctors and prices yourself through the admin panel. It is best to check with a lawyer what exactly the order requires of your clinic. If the lawyer says you need a section the site does not have, we name the price before we start. Online booking, where a patient picks a doctor and a time, costs extra; the price is in the “Options” list on this page. Without it, a patient leaves a request on the site and it comes to your Telegram and email. For clinics we also have the “Site for your industry” plan: we take the sections from our demo and draw the design for you. It will be cheaper and faster than “Business” if those sections and appointment requests are enough for you: the “Site for your industry” plan has no online booking with a choice of time.

process.title: Style, pages and what goes on them
process.text: Before the start we need a signed contract, the 30% prepayment and the materials from our list. Did not gather the materials in time? We move the start to the nearest free date, and the prepayment is not lost. No texts of your own? We write them from a questionnaire and a conversation with you, and the deadline grows by 4 days: we still show the styles 2 working days after the prepayment, with headings from the questionnaire, and write the texts once you pick a style. After the prepayment we draw the top of your home page in three styles. You pick one or take a ready-made style: one of the five styles of this site or the style of our demo. We show three styles 2 working days after the prepayment and the materials, and three more 2 working days after your reply. These dates also go into the contract, and for each working day we are late with the styles we also cut the price by 2%, within the same overall cap of 20%. The deadline runs from the day you pick a style. In the first two days we decide together which pages there will be (up to seven) and what goes on each.

process.title: Design of the home page and other pages
process.text: We draw the home page and the other pages in the chosen style and show them to you. You send your comments in one list: that is the first of three rounds of revisions.

process.title: All the pages and the admin panel
process.text: We build all the pages, the admin panel, the lead forms and analytics. The site runs on a temporary link: you check it and send the second list of comments. We make them, and then you make the second payment of 40%.

process.title: Testing and launch
process.text: You send the third and final list of comments, and we make them. We move the site to your web address (domain). We test the speed with Google's test on your address and attach the result to the acceptance certificate. If it is below 90, we find the cause and show it to you. We set up the hosting, so its speed is our concern: we fix it for free. If a third-party widget you chose slows the site down, we already told you before the contract what score we promise. We give you a guide and a screencast: how to change texts, photos and prices in the admin panel and read leads. You accept the work and pay the final 30%. Then comes a one-year warranty.

faq.question: What does “Telegram and MAX for one price” mean for a custom app?
faq.answer: We write the app once and connect it to two messengers, Telegram and MAX. That is why the second messenger costs nothing extra: a custom app works in both for one price. The industry app is different: the price includes only Telegram, and MAX is added for a separate fee. For MAX you register your company (we send instructions). MAX reviews the app, and that time is not part of our deadline.

faq.question: Which modules can I add?
faq.answer: Booking, loyalty, a showcase with ordering, and a referral program. We settle the set at the brief.

faq.question: Why is the price “from”?
faq.answer: Every project has its own modules and integrations. We name the exact amount after the brief.

faq.question: What does the plan include besides the app itself?
faq.answer: A Telegram bot your customers open the app through, and an admin panel, the section where you change texts, photos and prices yourself and see bookings, orders and bonuses. Everything else included in the price is in the “What is included” list on this page. The exact deadline, 3 to 4 weeks from the day you pick the style, we name once we discuss your task and put it in the contract.

process.title: The task, features and choosing a style

These dates also go into the contract, and for each working day we are late with the styles we also cut the price by 2%, within the same overall cap of 20%. None of the three fit? We draw three more. None of those fit either? We refund the whole prepayment. The contract deadline starts the day you pick a style.

faq.question: How many products can I upload?
faq.answer: The plan includes a catalog of up to 100 products. If you have more, we price the extra ones separately.

faq.question: Can customers pay for an order and choose delivery on the site?
faq.answer: Yes. A customer puts products in the cart, pays on the site and chooses delivery. You see the orders in the order admin panel, the section where you process them. Which service takes the payments (Stripe, for example) and which company delivers, we decide together when we discuss your task.

faq.question: Why is the price “from”?
faq.answer: Every store has its own catalog, simpler or more complex, and its own set of connections to other services, such as payment and delivery. We name the exact amount once we discuss your task.

faq.question: Who manages the orders?
faq.answer: You do, in the order admin panel, the section where all the orders are visible. We send a guide and a screencast on how to use it.

You pick one or take a ready-made style: one of the five styles of this site. These dates also go into the contract, and for each working day we are late with the styles we also cut the price by 2%, within the same overall cap of 20%. None of the three fit? We draw three more. None of those fit either? We refund the whole prepayment. The contract deadline starts the day you pick a style. You send the product catalog by the date we put in the contract.

faq.question: What is an MVP in your plan?
faq.answer: An MVP is the first working version of your service, with only the essentials. Users sign in with a login and password, and each has their own account. People can pay in the service, it is connected to the other services you need, and it collects statistics. With this version you can test the idea with real users.

faq.question: Why does it take 6–10 weeks?
faq.answer: The deadline depends on how many different kinds of user accounts the service has (for example, for customers and for staff) and how many connections to other services it needs. We put the exact deadline in the contract once we discuss your task.

faq.question: Who owns the code?
faq.answer: You. We hand over the source code, all the files the service is built from, together with the passwords. With it you can change the service and move to another developer without us.

faq.question: What happens after launch?
faq.answer: For a year from the day of acceptance we fix for free anything that broke through our fault or does not work the way the contract says. Looking after the server, making backups and updating software is support, and you can add it right after launch. Or a Dev subscription: $3,500 a month, we work through your tasks one at a time, with no limit on the number of tasks.

process.title: The task, the first version and choosing a style
process.text: Before the start we go through the brief in writing: what the service should do and decide what goes into the first version. In reply we send the estimate, the deadline and a draft contract. After the 30% prepayment we draw the main screen of the service in three styles: colors, fonts, the look of buttons and blocks. You pick one or take a ready-made style: one of the five styles of this site. We show three styles 2 working days after the prepayment and the materials for the main screen from our list, and three more 2 working days after your reply. These dates also go into the contract, and for each working day we are late with the styles we also cut the price by 2%, within the same overall cap of 20%. None of the three fit? We draw three more. None of those fit either? We refund the whole prepayment. The contract deadline starts the day you pick a style.

process.title: Design and how the service works
process.text: We draw the account screens, work out what data the service stores and list the connections to other services (integrations). You send your comments in one list: that is the first of three rounds of revisions.

process.title: We build the service in parts
process.text: We build the service in parts: sign-in, user accounts, payments, connections to other services and analytics. We show interim versions on a temporary link. You send the second list of comments. We make them, and then you make the second payment of 40%.

process.title: Testing and launch
process.text: We make your third and final list of comments. We check the whole user journey from start to finish: sign-in, account, payment. We launch. We hand over all the passwords and the source code, the files the service is built from. We test the speed with Google's test on the pages listed in the contract: it needs 90 out of 100 or more, and the result goes with the acceptance certificate. If it is below 90, we find the cause and show it to you. We set up the hosting, so its speed is our concern: we fix it for free. If a third-party widget you chose slows the site down, we already told you before the contract what score we promise. You sign the acceptance certificate and pay the final 30%. Then comes a one-year warranty.

process.title: Brief and materials
process.text: Before day one you send a short written description of the task. If you have a 3D model of the product (a file from a drawing program, CAD), attach it. If there is no model, send photos and drawings. If you need it, we sign an NDA before you send the files. In reply we send the estimate, the deadline, the nearest free date and a draft contract. All of it before you pay anything. Then you make the 30% prepayment and send a detailed description with photos and videos of the parts, the components and mechanisms the scene will show. Our questions about the parts come as one list. For a 3D landing page we draw three styles after the prepayment: the background and lighting of the scene, the colors of the labels and the look of the page around it. You pick one or take a ready-made style: one of the five styles of this site. We show three styles 2 working days after the prepayment and the materials, and three more 2 working days after your reply. These dates also go into the contract, and for each working day we are late with the styles we also cut the price by 2%, within the same overall cap of 20%. None of the three fit? We draw three more. None of those fit either? We refund the whole prepayment. A 3D block goes into your site, so its style is matched to the site, with no separate choice. Day one of the work is the day we have the detailed description and the materials, and for a 3D landing page also the chosen style.

process.title: The shape of the model and viewing angles
process.text: We sign off the model, the camera angles and the parts the scene explains with you. The scene is built after the sign-off.

process.title: The 3D scene and labels
process.text: We build the scene, a camera move to every part, labels and the inquiry form inside the scene. For a 3D block this step is week 2.

process.title: Loading image, phones, speed test
process.text: We make the image a visitor sees while the 3D loads. For phones that cannot show 3D (no WebGL 2.0), we make an image and a video instead of the scene. We run Google's free speed test in advance. We show the scene on a temporary link. For a 3D landing page this step also includes the page around the scene. For a 3D block this step is week 3.

process.title: Revisions and launch
process.text: You send comments and we make them, up to three rounds. After we make the second-round revisions, you make the second payment of 40%. We launch and hand over all the project files. On launch day we test the speed again: Google's test on a phone has to show 90 out of 100 or more. For a 3D landing page we test it on your address; for a 3D block, the page with the scene on our temporary link, as the terms say. The result goes with the acceptance certificate. You accept the work and pay the final 30%. Then comes a one-year warranty. For a 3D block this step is week 4.

faq.question: We don't have a 3D model — what now?
faq.answer: We build one from scratch using photos and drawings. It is a separate line in both the estimate and the schedule, priced before any prepayment so the cost does not change mid-project.

faq.question: How does 3D work on older phones?
faq.answer: First the visitor sees a regular image of the model, and the 3D loads after it. If a phone cannot show 3D (it lacks the WebGL 2.0 technology), it shows an image and a video instead, and the inquiry form works either way. On a weak phone the model may rotate more slowly, but the image, the labels and the inquiry form are there right away.

faq.question: How much do revisions cost after three lists of comments?
faq.answer: Three rounds of revisions are included: texts, colors and highlights. After that each change is paid by the hour: we name the amount first, and you never pay more than that. We charge $90 an hour. Once you approve the shape of the model itself, we do not change it as part of revisions. If you need to show a new part or a new viewing angle, we name the price first and then do it.

faq.question: Can you put 3D on Tilda, WordPress or 1C-Bitrix?
faq.answer: No. We only work with sites written in code, not put together on Tilda, WordPress or 1C-Bitrix. We embed a 3D block into such a site: yours, if developers wrote it without a website builder, or one we built. If your site is on a website builder, we can make a 3D landing page, a separate page with its own address, such as 3d.yoursite.com, and link to it from your site.

faq.question: What is the difference between a 3D block and a 3D landing page?
faq.answer: A 3D block is one 3D model that we embed into a site written in code: yours or one we built. A 3D landing page is a separate one-page site with the model at its center. We write the texts for it from your answers to our questions. The page has an inquiry form and everything from the “Included in the price of every site” list, site visit statistics included.

faq.question: Can someone download our model from the site?
faq.answer: Yes, like any image on a website. That is why the site gets a lightweight display copy: the outside look and the parts you approved for display, without the other internal details, tolerances or drawings. We never share the drawings or the source model with third parties.

faq.question: What does support include?
faq.answer: Support is optional. There are four plans. The first is “Hosting and backups”, {hostingBackups} a month. That pays for our work: we look after the server the site runs on, check that the site opens, make backups and update the software. Changes to the site are not included. You pay for the server itself (the hosting) to the provider separately. The other three plans are all of the same plus hours of our work on changes to the site: {supportHours} a month for 3 hours, {supportHoursPlus} for 10 hours, {supportHoursPro} for 25 hours. Unused hours do not carry over. On every plan, if the site stops working, we get on it within 2 hours on weekdays from 10:00 to 19:00 Moscow time, and at night or on weekends the first working morning. Restoring the site after a failure, including from a backup, is part of the monthly fee.

faq.question: Where is the site hosted and who pays for it?
faq.answer: The site runs on a server of a hosting provider; that is the hosting. The account with the provider is in your name, and you pay the provider directly. Prices depend on the provider and can change. We set up the server and look after it, and all the passwords stay with you.

faq.question: What if the hours of edits run out?
faq.answer: Then extra work is paid by the hour, $90 an hour. If changes are many and constant, you can switch to a Dev subscription: $3,500 a month, we work through your tasks one at a time, with no limit on the number of tasks.

faq.question: How do I pay for support?
faq.answer: Every month: the price on this page is the fee for one month. You can cancel in any month: just don't pay for the next one.

process.title: Watching the site and backups
process.text: We make sure the site opens. We make regular backups so the site can be restored after a failure. Restoring the site after a failure, including from a backup, is part of the monthly fee. If the site stops working, we get on it within 2 hours on weekdays from 10:00 to 19:00 Moscow time, and at night or on weekends the first working morning.

process.title: Updating the site's software
process.text: We update the software the site runs on so it keeps up with new versions.

process.title: If something needs changing
process.text: You tell us what to change. On the plans with hours we do it out of the hours included in the fee: 3, 10 or 25 hours a month. The {hostingBackups} plan has no hours, so the work is billed separately at $90 an hour. Bugs that are our fault we fix for free during the warranty year, without spending your hours.

meta.title: Privacy policy
meta.description: What data the MRSHKN studio website collects, why, where it goes and how to withdraw your consent.

operator.title: Who processes your data
paragraphs: The data controller is Veronika Viktorovna Murashkina, a self-employed professional in Russia trading as MRSHKN studio (taxpayer ID 421815967902).
For any question about your data, email hello@mrshkn.com.

data.title: What data we collect
paragraphs: From the request you send through the brief on this website:
items: your name;
how to reach you: phone, email or messenger handle;
your brief answers: what you need built, industry, style, timing, budget and comments;
campaign tags, if you came from an ad.

purposes.title: Why we process it
paragraphs: We use request data to reply to you, discuss your project and prepare a proposal.
We use analytics data to see website traffic and understand which pages and ads work.

basis.title: Legal basis
paragraphs: We process your data based on your consent. You consent to the processing of your request by ticking the box in the brief before sending it, and to analytics cookies by clicking “Accept” in the cookie banner.

transfer.title: Where your data goes
paragraphs: Your whole request — name, contact details, brief answers and campaign tags — is saved in the website's database. It can only be opened from the site's admin panel, after signing in with a login and password.

The name and contact details from your request, together with your brief answers, are sent to Telegram: the studio's bot posts a notification about each new request to the studio's group chat. The site's server reaches Telegram through Cloudflare, so these details pass through Cloudflare on their way to Telegram. Telegram and Cloudflare are services based outside Russia.
A copy of your request is emailed to hello@mrshkn.com, the studio mailbox hosted by Yandex.
Analytics data goes to Yandex (Yandex Metrica) and Google (Google Analytics 4), and only after you consent. Google is a service based outside Russia.

storage.title: Where and how long data is stored
paragraphs: The website and its database run on a Timeweb Cloud server in Novosibirsk, Russia.
We keep request data for as long as we need it to reply and work on your project. Email hello@mrshkn.com and we will delete it sooner.

cookies.title: Cookies and analytics
paragraphs: Yandex Metrica and Google Analytics 4 only start after you click “Accept” in the cookie banner. Until then your browser does not contact them, and after “Decline” they never load.
Without analytics, the website sets only its own cookies: your banner choice, the style and theme you picked and, if you came from an ad, campaign tags so they reach your request.
You can change your mind at any time: use the button below and the banner will appear again.

rights.title: Your rights
paragraphs: Email hello@mrshkn.com if you want to:
items: find out what data we hold about you;
correct or delete it;
withdraw your consent to the processing of your request.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: This policy may change. The current version is always on this page, with the date at the top.

consent.summary: Your signature, business, link and review text will appear on the studio’s website. Your full name and email are not published, and you can withdraw consent by email.
items: Who gives consent: the author of the review — the full name entered in this form; contact email — the address the invitation was sent to.
To whom: [Full name], self-employed (professional income tax payer), Tax ID [Tax ID], address: [Address], email hello@mrshkn.com (the “Operator”).
Purpose: publishing my review of the work of MRSHKN studio so that visitors to the website can read it.

Where it is published: the website https://mrshkn.com — the home page (https://mrshkn.com/ru, https://mrshkn.com/en) and the case page of my project (https://mrshkn.com/ru/work/[case address], https://mrshkn.com/en/work/[case address]). The review is published in the language it was written in. A translation is published only after I have approved its text in writing, labelled “translation approved by the author”.

What is published: my name as I entered it in the “How to sign the review” field; my business or job title; a link to a website or page, if I provided one; the text of the review — answers to three questions. The full name from item 1 and the contact email are not published. Photos are neither collected nor published.

Conditions and prohibitions (optional, Part 9 of Article 10.1 of Federal Law No. 152-FZ “On Personal Data”) are set with the checkboxes in the form: a ban on transferring the data to third parties other than for publication on the website from item 4; a ban on publishing the link from item 5; other conditions. If nothing is checked, no conditions or prohibitions are set. An unchecked consent box does not count as consent (Part 8 of Article 10.1 of the Law).
Term: this consent is valid until withdrawn.

How to withdraw: email hello@mrshkn.com from the address in item 1, stating your full name, email and which data to remove (all or some). The Operator removes the review from the website within 3 (three) business days of receiving the request (Part 14 of Article 10.1 of the Law).

mail.subject: {project}: three questions from MRSHKN studio
paragraphs: Hello,

This is MRSHKN studio. We built {project} together, and we would like to know how the work looks from your side. We will show your review on the studio's website — it will tell new clients more than anything we could say.

The form has three questions: what brought you to us, how the work went and what changed after launch. The third question is optional: if little time has passed since launch, you can skip it. Answer as you like, short or long — we publish criticism too and only fix typos. It takes about ten minutes, no sign-up or passwords:
{link}
The form asks for your full name only for the consent — it will not appear on the site. The review is signed the way you choose, for example “Anna, coffee shop on Main Street”.

You can send the review only with consent to publish it — there are two checkboxes at the end of the form. If you change your mind, reply to this email and we will take it down. If the project was done at the case-study price, what happens to the discount follows the terms of your contract.
The link works for 60 days. Thank you for the project.
MRSHKN studio
